negatives.actualObservation: Read the entire current registered artifact. It walks through nine adjacent term entries with repeated definition, comparison, In real life and role-sentence moves. Team, taxi, Clueless wardrobe, Walkman, toolbox, collage and Miss Jeeves compete for attention without one request developing across the parts. The opening command supplies terminology before a learner-owned problem. Individual role assertions do not show how to find and repair a failure; the promised what-to-fix payoff is unearned. The repeated instructional structure becomes dry despite references.

evidence.excerpt: We will begin with one decision and follow it all the way through.
Later chapters will open each part carefully

negatives.actualObservation: Read the entire current registered artifact. Northstar and Juniper carry a connected and understandable technical diagnosis, but the broad book is framed around fixing one private decision. The opening does not establish judging public hype or informed participation before tracing context, inference and tools. The worked example dominates; the final future-topic list returns to machinery rather than earning the missing civic and public-claim motivations. Reject for the foundational destination, while retaining the useful causal explanation as a strength rather than pretending every sentence is poor.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: The Gates Foundation is pledging $1 billion over two years for AI access in health, education, agriculture and local languages, AP reported on September 15.

sourceEvidence.excerpt:
L1794: NEW YORK (AP) — cite190†Bill Gates is warning technology companies and world leaders that they must act now to ensure artificial intelligence combats social inequities rather than deepening disparities — and his foundation is pledging $1 billion to improve access.
L1795: The Microsoft co-founder made the appeal in cite191†the Gates Foundation’s annual Goalkeepers report , which tracks progress on the development goals set by the United Nations to improve quality of life by 2030. The donation announced Tuesday will be spread over the next two years for AI-focused efforts to train models on local languages, improve health outcomes, upgrade educational tools and cite192†inform small farmers’ practices around the world.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: AP report dated September15; exact announcement date deliberately not resolved. Pledge not expenditure.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: AI tools need to work in local languages and reflect local circumstances.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: L335: This requires investment in local language datasets and evaluations tailored to how people use language in the places these tools are meant to serve.

L343: The same is true in health. Global health guidelines already exist. The work now is making those guidelines locally relevant: incorporating the right epidemiology for a specific country, the treatment options actually available in that health system, the operating conditions of the clinics where health workers are making decisions.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: Foundation stated rationale, not proof of benefit; health-worker example explicitly hypothetical.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Its proposed goal is useful support for health workers, teachers and farmers, rather than replacing their judgment.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: L203: Of course, healthcare workers, farmers, and teachers should continue to bring their unique judgment, creativity, and care to their work. But designed well, AI can give them more support, helping knowledge travel farther, faster.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: Attributed proposed goal, not product guarantee.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: AP quotes University of Vermont sociologist Jonathan Shaffer warning that marginalized people may remain missing from the data and weak health infrastructure remains a barrier.

sourceEvidence.excerpt:
L1836: More data won’t guarantee more equitable tools, according to Jonathan Shaffer, an assistant professor of sociology at the University of Vermont. Shaffer, whose research focuses on how global health governance is shaped by science and knowledge, noted that health infrastructure is extraordinarily weak in many parts of the world.
L1837: The most marginalized populations would likely remain excluded from the data fed into health-oriented AI models, he suggested, which “may even amplify the kinds of inequalities” the foundation aims to reduce.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: Shaffer independent warning, not foundation admission or established measured outcome.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Many promising tools are still pilots, the foundation says.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: L241: Today, many of the most promising AI tools are still in pilot mode. They need to work in all languages, on ordinary phones, and in the places where people make real-life decisions before they can be trusted to take to scale. But the distance between pilot mode and scale could be much shorter than it was for earlier technologies—because if done well, AI can reach people through natural conversation, on a device already in their pocket.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: Foundation claim; no specific effectiveness metric repeated.
